boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Carleton spaces for studying, gathering, making, recreation, reflection, and student-facing events, each grounded in a direct institutional source.

cards.title: Use the Open Lab Between Classes
cards.subtitle: A flexible work stop inside Gould Library
cards.notes: Check whether Library 306 is between instruction sessions, then use its open computer lab for focused work or printing.
cards.short_summary: A library classroom doubles as an open computer lab when it is not scheduled for instruction.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s library tour identifies Room 306 as a library classroom that operates as an open computer lab when it is not in use.
cards.source_title: Classrooms and Computer Labs — Library Tour
cards.access_notes: Room 306 is available as an open lab only when it is not scheduled for library instruction.

cards.title: Meet in the Campus Center’s Main Room
cards.subtitle: The shared interior hub of Sayles-Hill
cards.notes: Use Great Space as a visible meetup point before checking nearby student activities, mail services, or campus-center events.
cards.short_summary: Sayles-Hill’s central room connects everyday meetups with several student-facing services.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s facilities plan identifies Great Space as the core of the Sayles-Hill Campus Center and describes it as welcoming students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: Campus-center entry and individual services may follow current college access rules and operating schedules.

cards.title: Take Reading Outside
cards.subtitle: The central lawn beside Sayles-Hill
cards.notes: Bring a book or Frisbee when conditions are dry; the open lawn works for an outdoor study break or informal recreation.
cards.short_summary: The central lawn supports both quiet reading and casual student activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s official image archive documents students studying on the Bald Spot in fall 2023.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use depends on weather, grounds conditions, and any scheduled campus activity.

cards.title: Choose Your Own Kind of Movement
cards.subtitle: Courts, track, climbing, and fitness under one roof
cards.notes: Check the recreation schedule, then choose an open-use court, the indoor track, a fitness area, or an appropriate climbing option.
cards.short_summary: One facility accommodates several forms of individual and group recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton Athletics states that the Recreation Center supports recreation including basketball, tennis, weightlifting, rock climbing, aerobics, and racquet sports.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current building hours, eligibility, reservations, supervision, and equipment requirements before participating.

cards.title: Pick a Trail That Fits the Day
cards.subtitle: The campus-side section of Cowling Arboretum
cards.notes: Consult the trail map before walking, running, skiing, or biking, and keep bicycles only on designated Upper Arb routes.
cards.short_summary: The Upper Arb offers a denser trail network close to campus for several kinds of recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s Arboretum trail map says visitors use its trails for hiking, running, limited biking, cross-country skiing, and nature appreciation.
cards.source_title: Cowling Arboretum Trail Map and Visitor Rules
cards.access_notes: Stay on trails, leash dogs, do not camp, and observe seasonal archery-hunt restrictions and posted rules.

cards.title: Bake in a House Built Around Hospitality
cards.subtitle: A small campus house with a student baking culture
cards.notes: Check the house’s current access guidance before visiting, then leave the kitchen and shared rooms ready for the next group.
cards.short_summary: A domestic-scale campus space has long brought students together through baking, music, conversation, and study breaks.
cards.evidence_claim: A Carleton-hosted study of Dacie Moses House documents students baking cookies and muffins, studying, playing music, talking, and gathering there.
cards.source_title: A Study of Dacie Moses House
cards.access_notes: Historical descriptions do not establish present-day unrestricted access; verify current house guidance before entering or using the kitchen.

cards.title: Work Where the Sciences Intersect
cards.subtitle: The central shared space in Evelyn M. Anderson Hall
cards.notes: Use an available workspace between classes, and keep circulation routes clear around the atrium’s connecting stairs and ramps.
cards.short_summary: The science complex’s central atrium combines circulation, student work areas, and public academic exchange.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s campus-history project says the Anderson Hall atrium connects three science buildings and contains multiple student workspaces.
cards.source_title: A History of Science Facilities at Carleton
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to current building access, class schedules, posted events, and any reserved portions of the atrium.

cards.title: Browse the Environmental Studies Lounge
cards.subtitle: A student-use common room inside Goodsell Observatory
cards.notes: Drop in to browse reading material, look for internship information, or connect with others when the lounge is open.
cards.short_summary: Goodsell’s Room 106 provides Environmental Studies students with readings, opportunity information, and a place to meet.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s Environmental and Technology Studies page identifies Goodsell Observatory Room 106 as a lounge for reading material, internships, and meeting people.
cards.access_notes: The source does not provide current hours or unrestricted visitor access; confirm availability with the program before visiting.

cards.title: Use the Chapel for Reflection and Dialogue
cards.subtitle: A campus setting for worship, meditation, and discussion
cards.notes: Review the Chaplain’s Office calendar, choose a suitable gathering, and respect the practices and quiet use of each room.
cards.short_summary: The Chapel supports religious and interfaith gatherings as well as meditation and discussion.
cards.evidence_claim: A Carleton advising bulletin says the Chaplain’s Office hosts weekly worship, meditation, and discussion events, including interfaith programs open to everyone.
cards.source_title: The Bi-Weekly Advising Bulletin — Weeks 5–6, Fall Term 2019
cards.access_notes: Event schedules and room availability change; consult current Chaplain’s Office information before attending.

cards.title: See Coursework Become Public Conversation
cards.subtitle: A presentation space inside the science complex
cards.notes: Look for posted public presentations, give presenters room to explain their work, and avoid interrupting nearby classes.
cards.short_summary: The atrium can turn a class project into a public exchange with students and passersby.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s Digital Humanities in Classics site documents a Spring 2024 course holding its final public poster session in Anderson Atrium.
cards.source_title: Race: Antiquity and Its Legacy — Spring 2024
cards.access_notes: Poster sessions are scheduled events rather than permanent displays; check current event information before going.

warnings: Current public pages did not provide verifiable coordinates or stable map URLs for individual subjects, so those fields are null.
Several official sources document established uses but do not publish current access hours; those limitations are stated in access_notes.
